extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for NIH grants who need to prepare a resubmission
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for investigators whose NIH grant application was rejected, outlining emotional management, planning, contacting program officers, revising the application and introduction, updating literature, and avoiding common submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take a few days
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a few days after receiving your summary statement to calm your emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t take criticism personally. Allow time to process reviewer comments before responding or revising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the summary statement carefully and start making a plan for resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify what you can do quickly to address reviewers’ concerns (e.g., rewriting unclear sections, reviewing additional literature, conducting additional statistical analyses, or performing straightforward lab work) versus what will take longer. Use this to prioritize revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach out to your program officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators planning a resubmission should always contact their program officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email to set up a virtual or telephone meeting rather than cold calling. If possible, email specific questions, concerns, or an outline of revision plans so the program officer can prepare for the conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep up with your field
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised grants usually must be submitted within 37 months of the original application; keep up with recent literature and new technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If substantial time has passed, ensure the resubmission demonstrates reading recent literature and awareness of new technologies. Confirm that your science reflects current field advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond thoroughly and professionally
rubrics_metrics.description: In the introduction to your resubmission, summarize the reviewers’ criticisms and then address them all politely and constructively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers of resubmissions have access to the original summary statement and consider whether prior concerns have been adequately addressed. If you can’t address a concern or disagree with it, explain why rather than ignore it. The introduction should clearly indicate what has changed in the resubmitted proposal. Note: NIH no longer requires marking changes in the Research Strategy document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek advice from mentors and colleagues who have been through resubmission and those who served on study sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People outside your immediate field can help with clarity. Use editors (e.g., Research Medical Library editors) to improve readability and organization of your proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with your strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the weaknesses identified by reviewers while being careful not to change elements the reviewers liked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight ongoing work by including new findings or new preliminary data to strengthen the resubmission and leverage existing positive reviewer perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reread the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-read the FOA to ensure it still applies at the time of resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many NIH FOAs expire after 3 years; most allow resubmissions but some do not. Confirm the FOA’s eligibility and any changes. (NIH tip: check FOA 30 days before submitting.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid several common errors that reduce chances of receiving a fundable score, such as not contacting your program officer and failing to respond thoroughly to reviewers' comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize clear communication, including visual communication. Write clearly and organize well; use bold text sparingly to highlight important points and review criteria. Keep paragraphs short and tightly focused. Ensure figures and legends are clear and readable and the page layout makes good use of white space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t give up
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, it’s a good idea to revise and resubmit an unfunded proposal; NIH data show resubmitted applications have higher success rates than initial submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless reviewers found major problems across several review criteria (which may require reconceptualizing the study), consider resubmitting rather than abandoning the project.
